body.statement: For sample sizes in the deterministic eventual regime \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal M}T_n(P)\ge T_0\), the sets \(\mathcal C_n(a)\) are intervals, and \(\Pr_P\{\theta(a)\in\mathcal C_n(a)\text{ for all }a\in J\}\to1-\alpha\) uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal M\). The image construction in \(\texttt{def:crossing-set}\) is therefore an eventual-regime simultaneous \((1-\alpha)\)-level confidence set for \(\tau_{\zeta}\) for every fixed \(\zeta\), including the empty and all-domain conventions.
body.justification: Joint LR calibration should report the scientifically interpretable crossing doses and the whole curve with one common coverage event.
body.gap: Doss (2026) reports pointwise LR intervals in the nurse-staffing application; the proposition uses a genuinely simultaneous LR critical value and a coverage-preserving inverse map.
body.consumer: AHA/CMS analysts can report the nurse-hours level at which the readmission profile crosses a policy-relevant threshold with simultaneous uncertainty.

obligation.what_is_open: The deterministic inversion is proved, but its nominal limiting coverage awaits \(\texttt{thm:feasible-calibration}\).
obligation.obstruction: Convexity and the set-image argument preserve whatever coverage the common LR event has; they cannot establish that the unresolved common critical value has probability \(1-\alpha\).
obligation.attempted: The constrained value function was shown convex, the band event was shown exactly equal to the supremum event, and the monotone crossing image was shown coverage preserving, including empty and endpoint cases.
obligation.partial_result:
For a fixed data index \(k\), write
\[
 L_k(t)=\min_{u\in\mathcal C_n,\,u_k=t}\sum_{i=1}^n(Z_{(i)}-u_i)^2.
\]
The feasible set is nonempty because it contains the constant vector \(t\mathbf 1\).  Joint convexity of the squared loss and affinity of the constraint imply that \(L_k\) is convex in \(t\).  Consequently \(Q_n(a,t)=L_{k(a)}(t)-\min_{u\in\mathcal C_n}\sum_i(Z_{(i)}-u_i)^2\) is convex in \(t\), and every sublevel set \(\mathcal C_n(a)\) is an interval, allowing the empty interval and \(\mathbb R\).  Positivity of \(\widehat\kappa\) gives the exact event identity
\[
 \{\theta(a)\in\mathcal C_n(a)\ \forall a\in J\}
 =\left\{\sup_{a\in J}\frac{Q_n(a,\theta(a))}{\widehat\kappa(a)}
 \le\widehat q_{n,\alpha}\right\}
 =\{S_n(\theta)\le\widehat q_{n,\alpha}\}.
\]
On this event, the monotone true curve is one of the selectors used in \(\texttt{def:crossing-set}\), so its crossing value \(\tau_\zeta\) belongs to the image confidence set, including the stated endpoint conventions.  Thus the inversion step itself loses no coverage; only the unresolved calibration probability prevents the frozen proposition from being completed.
